[HIGH] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48` — Team authorization uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, excluding ordinary admins where either role should suffice.

[HIGH] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-165` — Calendar synchronization uses the invoking attendee/admin’s credentials instead of the booking owner’s, so non-organizer requests can fail after database persistence or target the wrong integration.

[HIGH] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-106,165` — Attendees are committed before the external calendar update. If synchronization fails, retries reject those addresses as existing, leaving the database and calendar permanently inconsistent.

[MEDIUM] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:3-5` — The server does not normalize or deduplicate submitted emails; duplicate input, case variants, or concurrent requests can create duplicate attendees or cause constraint failures.

[MEDIUM][A04] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-77` — Blacklist entries are lowercased but submitted addresses are not, allowing a case variant to bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`.

[MEDIUM] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168` — The mailer receives raw `guests` instead of filtered `uniqueGuests`; an existing attendee included with a new guest is misclassified and receives a fresh scheduling email.

[MEDIUM] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44-56` — No status/time guard prevents adding guests to cancelled, rejected, or completed bookings; the UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings at `BookingListItem.tsx:553-554`.

[MEDIUM] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58-68` — The handler queries user ID `0` when `booking.userId` is null, preventing ownerless/team-managed bookings from using the feature.

[MEDIUM][A04] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5` — The guest array is unbounded and duplicate-capable; an authorized attendee can trigger unbounded attendee creation, quadratic membership work, calendar processing, and parallel email fan-out.

[LOW/MEDIUM] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171` — Email failures are swallowed and success is returned without retry or actionable logging, allowing silent partial notification delivery.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [HIGH] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52-55` — Any attendee may add further guests; newly added guests become authorized attendees and can recursively extend the booking, broadening guest management beyond organizer/team control.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts lines 52-55, the authorization check is: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`. This means any attendee (isAttendee check at line 51: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)`) can add guests to a booking. When guests are added, they become attendees in the database (line 89-96 creates new attendees). This creates a recursive authorization issue: Guest A is added by organizer, Guest A can now add Guest B, Guest B can add Guest C, etc. This is a real security/authorization concern where the guest list can grow beyond the organizer's control, as any attendee gains the ability to add more attendees.

matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - the incorrect use of AND (&&) instead of OR (||) for team admin/owner permission checking. The candidate correctly points out that the logic 'isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)' excludes ordinary admins when either role should suffice, which is the same logical error described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [HIGH] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-165` — Calendar synchronization uses the invoking attendee/admin’s credentials instead of the booking owner’s, so non-organizer requests can fail after database persistence or target the wrong integration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts lines 158-165, the credentials are fetched using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` where `ctx.user` is the invoking user (could be an attendee or team admin), not necessarily the booking owner. The EventManager is then initialized with these credentials. However, the booking object already includes `user: { include: { credentials: true } }` which contains the booking owner's credentials. For calendar updates, using the wrong user's credentials could cause the update to fail or target the wrong calendar integration. This is a real correctness issue - when a team admin or attendee adds guests, the calendar update should use the organizer's credentials (booking.user.credentials) rather than the invoking user's credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [HIGH] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-106,165` — Attendees are committed before the external calendar update. If synchronization fails, retries reject those addresses as existing, leaving the database and calendar permanently inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real architectural issue. Looking at the code flow in addGuests.handler.ts: (1) Lines 92-106 update the database with new attendees via prisma.booking.update(), (2) Line 165 calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees() to sync with external calendar. If the calendar update fails, the database already has the new attendees committed. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) will exclude these emails since they now exist in booking.attendees, making it impossible to retry the calendar sync for those guests. This creates a permanent inconsistency where guests exist in the database but not in the external calendar. The error handling around sendAddGuestsEmails (lines 167-170) shows awareness of potential failures but the calendar sync has no such protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [MEDIUM] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44-56` — No status/time guard prevents adding guests to cancelled, rejected, or completed bookings; the UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings at `BookingListItem.tsx:553-554`.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code in the diff, the handler fetches the booking and checks permissions (isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, isAttendee), but there is no validation of the booking's status field or time. The code at lines 44-56 only checks if the booking exists and if the user has permission, but doesn't verify if booking.status is 'ACCEPTED'/'CONFIRMED' vs 'CANCELLED'/'REJECTED', nor does it check if the booking is in the past. This means guests could be added to cancelled, rejected, or already-completed bookings. The BookingListItem.tsx shows the 'add_members' action is added to the actions array without any conditional check for booking status or time. This is a real functional bug - the feature should logically prevent adding guests to bookings that are cancelled, rejected, or have already occurred.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [MEDIUM] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58-68` — The handler queries user ID `0` when `booking.userId` is null, preventing ownerless/team-managed bookings from using the feature.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 58-68 in addGuests.handler.ts, the code queries for the organizer with `id: booking.userId || 0`. If booking.userId is null, this queries for user ID 0, which likely doesn't exist. However, the code uses `findFirstOrThrow` which will throw an error if no user is found. This is actually a reasonable behavior - if there's no organizer (userId is null), the operation should fail. The booking was already fetched and includes the user relation, so if booking.userId is null, it means there's no organizer associated with the booking. The handler would throw an appropriate error rather than silently fail. Additionally, bookings typically always have a userId in Cal.com's data model. While the code could be cleaner (checking for null explicitly), this isn't a bug that would cause incorrect behavior - it would just result in a 'not found' error for edge cases that shouldn't normally occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [MEDIUM][A04] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5` — The guest array is unbounded and duplicate-capable; an authorized attendee can trigger unbounded attendee creation, quadratic membership work, calendar processing, and parallel email fan-out.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the schema in addGuests.schema.ts, the guests array is indeed unbounded (z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max() constraint). However, examining the handler in addGuests.handler.ts, there is duplicate filtering logic at lines 68-72 that filters out guests who are already attendees: `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))`. This addresses the duplicate-capable concern. However, the unbounded array concern is valid - there's no limit on how many guests can be added in a single request, which could lead to resource exhaustion through mass attendee creation, calendar updates, and email sending. The finding correctly identifies that the schema lacks bounds, though the duplicate filtering is actually present in the handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [LOW/MEDIUM] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171` — Email failures are swallowed and success is returned without retry or actionable logging, allowing silent partial notification delivery.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows lines 167-171 in addGuests.handler.ts where email sending failures are caught and only logged with 'console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")' before returning success. This is a real issue: the function returns {message: "Guests added"} even when emails fail to send, with no retry mechanism, no error details logged, and no indication to the user that notifications weren't delivered. This could lead to guests being added to bookings without receiving notification emails, which is a silent partial failure that users cannot detect or act upon.
